title: Backyard Habitat Hunt: Parent Guide
endLine: A habitat gives an animal food, water, air, shelter, and space.

scenes.tts: What lives in a patch of plain grass? Give your child ten minutes to look closely and test a guess. A string square gives you a place to start.
scenes.caption: What lives in a patch of plain grass? Give your child ten minutes to look closely and test a guess. A string square gives you a place to start.
scenes.visual: Warm, friendly schematic illustration of a sunny backyard lawn viewed from high above, looking like a smooth green carpet. The camera smoothly swoops down to grass-blade height, revealing a cutaway edge of brown soil below, gently swaying grass blades, a tiny ant carrying a crumb, and a small spider on a thread. Subject fills 70% of the frame.
scenes.narration: What lives in a patch of plain grass? Give your child ten minutes to look closely and test a guess. A string square gives you a place to start.

scenes.visual: Hold the same ground-level cutaway yard scene with soft drifting sunlight motes and swaying grass. Clean bold title appears over the open sky area: 'Backyard Habitat Hunt' with subtitle 'Parent Guide'.

scenes.tts: Here is what your child practices today. They practice slowing down, looking closely, and testing a guess with a count. They also sort living parts from nonliving parts. They discover one big idea. Every animal needs a habitat that supplies food, water, air, shelter, and space.
scenes.caption: Here is what your child practices today. They practice slowing down, looking closely, and testing a guess with a count. They also sort living parts from nonliving parts. They discover one big idea. Every animal needs a habitat that supplies food, water, air, shelter, and space.
scenes.visual: Same cutaway yard world. A crisp white string frame lights up around a patch of grass. As each need is named, a clean icon settles into the square: a crumb and seed (Food), a dewdrop on grass (Water), gentle breeze lines (Air), a tiny soil tunnel (Shelter), and a soft bracket across the square (Space). Labels are short, large, high-contrast.
scenes.narration: Here is what your child practices today. They practice slowing down, looking closely, and testing a guess with a count. They also sort living parts from nonliving parts. They discover one big idea. Every animal needs a habitat that supplies food, water, air, shelter, and space.

scenes.tts: Stay within arm's reach the whole time. Choose dry ground away from roads and water. Check for glass, sharp litter, and ant mounds. Keep pebbles, small pegs, and other small objects away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking.
scenes.caption: Stay within arm's reach the whole time. Choose dry ground away from roads and water. Check for glass, sharp litter, and ant mounds. Keep pebbles, small pegs, and other small objects away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking.
scenes.visual: Show an adult beside the child at a dry patch of grass away from a road and pond. The adult scans the ground and moves to a clear patch when they spot an ant mound. Show an open palm holding small items out of a younger child's reach.
scenes.narration: Stay within arm's reach the whole time. Choose dry ground away from roads and water. Check for glass, sharp litter, and ant mounds. Keep pebbles, small pegs, and other small objects away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking.

scenes.tts: Setup uses simple items. Bring about four and a half meters of string, four sticks, a pencil, and paper. Add a magnifying glass if you have one, plus garden gloves for rolling a log. Push the four sticks about one meter apart and wrap the string around them.
scenes.caption: Setup uses simple items. Bring about four and a half meters of string, four sticks, a pencil, and paper. Add a magnifying glass if you have one, plus garden gloves for rolling a log. Push the four sticks about one meter apart and wrap the string around them.
scenes.visual: Same yard cutaway widens slightly to show a tidy clipboard and illustrated supplies settling along the grass edge: coiled string, four corner sticks, a pencil, a magnifying glass, and adult garden gloves. Then the four sticks animate into the lawn corners, a schematic meter bar marks one side ('About 1 meter'), and the string wraps smoothly around all four sticks.
scenes.narration: Setup uses simple items. Bring about four and a half meters of string, four sticks, a pencil, and paper. Add a magnifying glass if you have one, plus garden gloves for rolling a log. Push the four sticks about one meter apart and wrap the string around them.

scenes.tts: Before you look, ask your child, “How many animals do you think we will find in our square?” Write down the guess. Then spend ten minutes looking closely. Part the grass gently with a pencil, and count each animal you see inside the string.
scenes.caption: Before you look, ask your child, “How many animals do you think we will find in our square?” Write down the guess. Then spend ten minutes looking closely. Part the grass gently with a pencil, and count each animal you see inside the string.
scenes.visual: Show a speech bubble beside the clipboard: 'How many animals do you think we will find in our square?' A pencil writes a question mark beside 'Guess'. Show an illustrated hand gently parting grass with a pencil. Tally each animal that appears inside the string.
scenes.narration: Before you look, ask your child, “How many animals do you think we will find in our square?” Write down the guess. Then spend ten minutes looking closely. Part the grass gently with a pencil, and count each animal you see inside the string.

scenes.tts: Now picture that square before you kneel. From up here, it looks like plain grass. What do you predict you will see moving in the square once you part the grass?
scenes.caption: Now picture that square before you kneel. From up here, it looks like plain grass. What do you predict you will see moving in the square once you part the grass?
scenes.visual: Pull back from the same string square so the grass looks plain and any animals stay hidden. Show a large card that reads, 'What will you see moving?'
scenes.narration: Now picture that square before you kneel. From up here, it looks like plain grass. What do you predict you will see moving in the square once you part the grass?

scenes.visual: Hold the card reading 'What will you see moving?' over the same string square for the silent pause. Let the grass sway slowly without revealing any animals.

scenes.tts: Here, parting the grass reveals an ant and a spider. Your square may look different with the season and weather. Grass itself is alive, too. When you finish looking, compare your count with your child’s guess.
scenes.caption: Here, parting the grass reveals an ant and a spider. Your square may look different with the season and weather. Grass itself is alive, too. When you finish looking, compare your count with your child’s guess.
scenes.visual: Fade the question card and move closer as a pencil gently parts the grass. Reveal an ant and a spider inside the string. Briefly highlight a blade of grass with the label 'Living'. Show the completed tally beside the guess on the clipboard.
scenes.narration: Here, parting the grass reveals an ant and a spider. Your square may look different with the season and weather. Grass itself is alive, too. When you finish looking, compare your count with your child’s guess.

scenes.tts: Next, help your child sort the square into two lists. List living things like grass and ants, and nonliving things like soil, rocks, and sunlight. Then pick one animal together. Ask, Where does this ant eat? Where could it find water? Together, trace its shelter and space.
scenes.caption: Next, help your child sort the square into two lists. List living things like grass and ants, and nonliving things like soil, rocks, and sunlight. Then pick one animal together. Ask, Where does this ant eat? Where could it find water? Together, trace its shelter and space.
scenes.visual: The clipboard slides forward alongside the yard cutaway and splits into two clean columns: 'Living' (grass blade, ant) and 'Nonliving' (soil, rock, sunbeam). Then the view focuses on one ant inside the cutaway: dotted leader lines connect the ant to crumbs and seeds ('Food'), a dewdrop ('Water'), a small underground tunnel ('Shelter'), and a bracket spanning the square and beyond ('Space').
scenes.narration: Next, help your child sort the square into two lists. List living things like grass and ants, and nonliving things like soil, rocks, and sunlight. Then pick one animal together. Ask, Where does this ant eat? Where could it find water? Together, trace its shelter and space.

scenes.tts: You can skip the log. If you look under one, have your child stand back while you put on garden gloves. Choose a light log and roll it toward you without lifting it. Look underneath, then gently roll it back into place.
scenes.caption: You can skip the log. If you look under one, have your child stand back while you put on garden gloves. Choose a light log and roll it toward you without lifting it. Look underneath, then gently roll it back into place.
scenes.visual: Pan to a light log at the edge of the square. Show the child standing back while gloved adult hands roll the log toward the adult without lifting it. Keep the log between the adult and the exposed soil. Show two pill bugs on the soil, then slowly roll the log back.
scenes.narration: You can skip the log. If you look under one, have your child stand back while you put on garden gloves. Choose a light log and roll it toward you without lifting it. Look underneath, then gently roll it back into place.

scenes.tts: Never put hands or feet where you cannot see. Step back if you see a snake. Watch animals where they are. Keep your hands off them. Never taste plants, berries, or mushrooms. Handle any glass lens yourself. Keep every magnifying glass pointed away from the sun.
scenes.caption: Never put hands or feet where you cannot see. Step back if you see a snake. Watch animals where they are. Keep your hands off them. Never taste plants, berries, or mushrooms. Handle any glass lens yourself. Keep every magnifying glass pointed away from the sun.
scenes.visual: Keep the string square in view. Show an eye icon beside a beetle with the label 'Look, do not touch'. Show crossed-out drawings of a leaf, berry, and mushroom. Then show an adult holding a magnifying glass angled down toward the grass, away from the sun.
scenes.narration: Never put hands or feet where you cannot see. Step back if you see a snake. Watch animals where they are. Keep your hands off them. Never taste plants, berries, or mushrooms. Handle any glass lens yourself. Keep every magnifying glass pointed away from the sun.

scenes.tts: Pull up the sticks and string, and put back any leaves you moved. Wash hands with soap and water and check for ticks afterward. Think back to the animal you watched. Its habitat is the place it finds what it needs.
scenes.caption: Pull up the sticks and string, and put back any leaves you moved. Wash hands with soap and water and check for ticks afterward. Think back to the animal you watched. Its habitat is the place it finds what it needs.
scenes.visual: Show an adult hand gathering the string and sticks and replacing a moved leaf. Briefly show icons for handwashing and a tick check. Then pull back to the undisturbed square so the ant can be seen moving near the grass and soil.
scenes.narration: Pull up the sticks and string, and put back any leaves you moved. Wash hands with soap and water and check for ticks afterward. Think back to the animal you watched. Its habitat is the place it finds what it needs.

scenes.line: A habitat gives an animal food, water, air, shelter, and space.
scenes.visual: Clean, calm end card tinted in warm deep green with the faint silhouette of grass blades gently swaying at the bottom edge. Centered in large high-contrast type: 'A habitat gives an animal food, water, air, shelter, and space.'
